findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: There were approximately three juvenile roaches and one adult roach observed to be in a cabinet in the front behind the registers. There were cardboard boxes in this cabinet and the PIC removed them during the inspection. Discussed reducing cardboard, as it acts as food for the roaches. The last two pest control treatments are from 9/25/2026 and 10/23/2026. The District Manager stated that they called the technician to ask for weekly treatments and the technician stated that this was impossible. Sentinel is supposed to be treating the facility biweekly according to the PIC, but the last two treatment dates are almost a month from each other. Discussed potentially switching pest control companies to receive more consistent treatment. Ensure that deep cleaning is continuing to be done, cardboard is being reduced, and that dead roaches are being cleaned up to allow for proper monitoring. A follow up is scheduled for 11/30/2026 to ensure that the appropriate actions are being taken to reduce pest presence.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: There were approximately four alive roaches and six dead roaches observed throughout the facility. There were no juvenile roaches observed. According to the PIC, Sentinel is currently treating the facility weekly. Discussed cleaning in the front kitchen more, as this is where all of the roaches were observed during the inspection. Facility has reduced the use of cardboard in areas where roaches were frequently spotted. Continue with this. Discussed making sure to clean up dead roaches to allow for better monitoring of the pest issue. A follow up is scheduled for 10/23/2026 to ensure that the facility is taking the appropriate measures to reduce pest presence in the facility, including but not limited to, cleaning, pest control, getting rid of cardboard, and cleaning up dead roaches. Ensure that the appropriate actions are being taken to reduce pest presence and to clean the facility.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: There were two alive roaches observed during the inspection, one by the wraps on the bottom of the cook-line and one on the wall behind the alto-shaams across from the cook-line. There were approximately 8 to 10 dead roaches observed throughout the facility. These alive and dead roaches were of varying life stages. The facility currently has Sentinel Pest Control coming weekly. There were no notes available from the pest control company. The facility has improved on cleaning and is continuing to work on it. The PIC also stated that they are working on getting rid of cardboard throughout the facility. A follow up is scheduled for 9/23/2026 to ensure that the facility is taking the appropriate measures to reduce pest presence in the facility, including but not limited to, cleaning, pest control, getting rid of cardboard, and cleaning up dead roaches. Ensure that the appropriate actions are being taken to reduce pest presence and clean the facility.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: There were multiple alive and dead roaches observed throughout the facility, including but not limited to, one alive roach on the cook-line, one dead in the bottom of the preparation cooler, one on a shelf of the cook-line, one dead and one alive on the bread rack, two alive on the wall behind the shake machine, and one alive in the cabinets under the soda machines in the lobby. These roaches were of different life stages and they were all fast-moving. According to the PIC, Sentinel, the facility’s pest control company, is currently coming every two weeks. The last receipt available was 7/16/2026 and there were no notes available from the pest control company. A follow up is scheduled for 8/18/2026 to ensure that the facility is taking the appropriate actions to reduce pest presence, including but not limited to, removing cardboard from the facility, using glue traps to monitor pest presence (no glue traps were observed), having pest control treat the facility, and cleaning floors and walls (accumulation of grease on them).

findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment:
There are single service containers on the cook line that are observed to be stored with the food contact surface exposed to contamination. Ensure that these containers are inverted to protect the food contact surface from contamination. 

There are fry containers in dispensers above the fryer that are observed to have their food contact surface facing the ceiling, where they are exposed to contamination. These containers either need to be inverted or have a covering on them to protect the food contact surface from contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: The facility had just ran out of sanitizer during the inspection. CORRECTED- The PIC was able to borrow and go get some more sanitizer from another store. A bucket was made and tested to be at the correct concentration during the inspection. Ensure that there is always sanitizer available during all hours of operation to make sure that surfaces are being properly sanitized. 

(B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: The Quat sanitizer water in the triple sink was tested to only be at a concentration of 100ppm. CORRECTED- The operator remade the sanitizer water and the buckets and the sanitizer tested to be at a concentration of 200ppm. Ensure that sanitizer water is frequently tested and changed if the concentration is below the recommended of between 200 and 400ppm. 

Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

An employee was observed to wash hands, turn off the faucet with their bare hands and then retrieve a paper towel for drying. Proper hand washing procedures were reviewed and the PIC is instructed to ensure that correct hand washing is taking place at all times.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

The three part sink would not register effective concentrations of Quat on the inspector’s test strips at the beginning of the inspection. Multiple attempts were made to troubleshoot the issue. The best attempt could get intermittent Quat out of the line but not enough to provide for sufficient concentration in solution for food contact surfaces. A solution was made manually using a CL based sanitizer of sufficient concentration. A new dispensing system is already at the facility and is waiting to be installed. Manually making the CL solution will be acceptable until the new dispenser is installed and calibrated. The inspector’s card was left with the PIC and thy are instructed to contact him when the new system is functional for a verification spot check.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

Four locations have the NUDO board pulling away from the wall. These locations need to be repaired so that there is not a gap and include: 1) to the right of the drive thru window; 2) the left of the doorway between the prep area and dish area; 3) the right of the doorway between the prep area and dish areas and; 4) the wall/corner to the left of the hand sink. Seal these locations so that the gap is eliminated.

If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.
